premises.statement: A rule or measure is applied to those who are regulated.
Law’s binding force is connected to application to its addressees.
Natural law is promulgated through natural insertion in minds.
The source describes natural law as naturally knowable.
A remote addressee is reached when promulgation comes or can come to knowledge through others.
Present promulgation extends into the future through durable writing.
Writing allows promulgation to continue through reading.
The definition gathers reason, common good, public care of community, and promulgation.
The objection argues natural law lacks promulgation and hence promulgation is not essential.
The objection argues promulgation to present hearers cannot account for others being bound.
The objection argues present promulgation cannot ground future obligation.
The sed contra says laws are instituted when promulgated.
An actual promulgation act occurred; this is separate from a remote addressee learning its content.
The law was promulgated in the present before the written record extended its reach into the future.
